method.purpose: Screen for dense/flattened, preserved peaks and exceptional peak contrast. These are project research criteria, not an industry DR rating or proof of mastering history.
method.signal: Original decoded recording at its native sample rate, all channels, no EQ/normalization/dynamics processing.
method.active_gate: 400ms RMS > max(-60 dBFS, full-track RMS - 20 dB). Loud passages are the upper quartile of active RMS/short-term LUFS windows; at least 60 seconds for firm screening.
method.peak_contrast: Stereo peak minus stereo RMS in nonoverlapping 50ms/400ms/3s windows, plus per-channel values; rolling aligned 3s true peak minus short-term LUFS (PSR).

categories.dense_flattened: Loud-passage median 400ms crest <=8 dB AND loud-passage median PSR <=8 dB, OR repeated peak plateaus (>=5 runs/min) with both loud-passage medians <=11 dB. The plateau branch detects flattening even when some transient contrast survives. Neither branch alone establishes the processing cause.
categories.exceptional_dynamics: Loud-passage median 400ms crest >=13 dB AND loud-passage median PSR >=13 dB AND at least 75% of loud 400ms windows have crest >=12 dB; no repeated plateau flag.
categories.preserved_peaks: Loud-passage median 400ms crest >=9 dB AND loud-passage median PSR >=9 dB; no repeated plateau flag. Below exceptional thresholds.
categories.review: All conflicting/borderline cases, repeated plateaus with higher contrast, and recordings shorter than 60 seconds remain unassigned; not forced into a fourth musical category.

method.flattening_flags: Gain-relative consecutive equal samples at >=95% of absolute file peak (tolerance peak*1e-7); >=5 runs of >=3 samples per minute flags repeated plateaus. Lossy decoding can obscure original flat tops; synthesis can create them. A flag is not proof of compression or audible damage.
method.limitations: No listening judgement or unprocessed reference assumed. Preserved/exceptional are measurement-screen candidates, not certification that every peak is untouched. LUFS/LRA/true peak retained as separate descriptors; format does not establish a distinct master.
